headline: Draft 2027-28 school calendar presented by assistant superintendent, starting September 1st, 2027.
summary: The draft shows a last day of June 15th, 2028, if there are no snow days, and the committee must schedule 185 school days. The vote to approve the calendar is likely at the next meeting, after a second reading. A motion asking administration to talk with SEU about a Monday start was tabled until legal advice comes back. The committee also approved the FY28 budget calendar, a $1,530 payment to Bunker Hill Community College, and most of policy manual section B.
decisions: Tabled a motion asking the administration to talk with SEU about a Monday start, until legal counsel gives advice.
Approved subcommittee reports from the October 19th, 20th and 21st meetings.
Approved the September and October bill rolls.
Approved policy manual section B, except BGB, BDFA-E, BEDH and BEDH-E.
Approved the FY28 budget development calendar.
Approved a $1,530 payment to Bunker Hill Community College for fiscal year 26 invoices, paid from fiscal year 27 funds.
Accepted donations of work boots for $30,000 and equipment for $1,580 for CTE programs.
Accepted an $18,000 grant for world language proficiency data.
discussion: 2027-28 school calendar: Members debated asking the administration to talk with SEU about a Monday start instead of the Wednesday, September 1st, 2027 start in the draft. The motion was tabled until legal counsel gives advice, and members were told the draft should not be distributed as an official calendar.

Student services screener: The director of student services said the BIMAS screener is in a second-year pilot, with a goal of all students taking it next year, subject to grant money. In the fall, she said two students scored high need and were evaluated with mental health professionals.

Policy manual section B: Members reviewed the Rules subcommittee's wording and agreed that advisory committee appointments will be made by the chair and approved by the full committee. The subcommittee will set a date for school improvement plans and rewrite the policy adoption steps in BGB, which members said was unclear.

Barr grant school leadership update: The superintendent presented early results from a Strengthening School Leadership Grant from the Barr Foundation, which works with three partners: Relay, TNTP and the Lynch Leadership Academy. The superintendent said these are early signs, not outcomes yet.

Public comment on injury: A parent said her son's hand was pulled into an industrial air purifier during class on January 28, and that the family got little support from school administrators. The parent said the accident report came only after she asked for it, and asked the committee to fix the process.
